chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the fasting person who brushes his teeth with water. He said: 'There is no problem with it.' And he said: 'He should not brush with a wet toothstick.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a fasting person to brush their teeth with water or a wet toothstick?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of siwak for the fasting individual, distinguishing between the permissibility of using water as a lubricant versus the potential invalidation caused by a pre-moistened stick absorbing moisture. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on preventing the ingestion of foreign substances, reflecting the broader principle of caution (ihtiyat) in maintaining the purity of the fast.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the Fasting-one who brushes the teeth with the water. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should not brush with the wet toothstick’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Um ay r from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who brushes his teeth with water. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful but one must not brush with a fresh twig.’”
